title: Tarta de Santiago
subtitle: The gluten-free Galician almond cake decorated with the cross of Saint James
excerpt: Tarta de Santiago is a single-layer almond cake with no flour, no leavening, and nothing more than ground almonds, eggs, sugar, lemon, and cinnamon. The batter takes five minutes to make. The result is dense, moist, and keeps well for four to five days. The cross of Saint James is stencilled on top with icing sugar.
sourceNotes: Tarta de Santiago (also Torta de Santiago) is a traditional cake from Galicia in north-west Spain, associated with the pilgrimage to Santiago de Compostela. The recipe has been protected by a European Geographic Indication since 2010. The cross of Saint James (the cross of the Order of Santiago) is the traditional decoration, applied as an icing-sugar stencil.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the icing-sugar decoration. Thaw at room temperature for 2 hours.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps well for 4 to 5 days at room temperature wrapped in baking paper. Add the icing-sugar decoration on the day of serving.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 180 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 165 degrees Celsius. Middle shelf. The top darkens quickly; tent with foil after 20 minutes if colouring too fast.

glossaryTerms.definition: The traditional icing-sugar decoration for tarta de Santiago. Print or draw the cross of the Order of Santiago on a piece of card, cut it out, lay the stencil on the cooled cake, and sift icing sugar over the top. Remove the stencil carefully to leave the cross shape defined in white on the dark almond surface.

content.text: Tarta de Santiago contains no flour, no butter, and no leavening. The eggs carry all the structure. Use good-quality almond flour or grind blanched almonds yourself; the fineness of the grind affects the texture. The
is the traditional decoration; it can be cut from a piece of card using a printed template.
Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius. Grease and line a 23 cm springform tin.
Whisk the eggs and caster sugar together for 3 to 4 minutes until thick and pale. Add the lemon zest, orange zest if using, and cinnamon. Fold in the almond flour until just combined.

Pour into the tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes. The top should be deep golden and a skewer inserted in the centre should come out clean with a few moist crumbs. Cover loosely with foil after 20 minutes if the top is darkening too quickly.
Cool completely in the tin. Unmould, lay the cross stencil on top, and sift icing sugar generously over the entire surface. Lift the stencil straight up to reveal the cross.
